summary: Iteration 12 frontend-only verification of the marquee continuity fix on the preview URL. The -50% keyframe change IS applied and correct (verified in stylesheet and via computed transform: track width 4064px desktop, translate sweeps 0 -> ~-2032px = exactly 50%). HOWEVER the marquee still goes BLANK: continuity sampling every 2.5s over a full 45s cycle gives 0/19 passing samples on BOTH 1440 and 390. New root cause found: the track is RIGHT-anchored because its containing block (.marquee-section) is RTL, so the max-content track overflows to the LEFT (inner.offsetLeft = -2624). Moving it further left empties the viewport from the right edge. Proven fix (validated live in-browser): make the containing block LTR — 19/19 samples then show FULL coverage (1440/1440 at every timestamp).

ui_bugs.issue: MARQUEE STILL GOES BLANK (bug persists despite the -50% fix). dir="ltr" is set on .marquee-inner, but its CONTAINING BLOCK (.marquee-section, inherits html dir=rtl) is RTL, so the width:max-content track is right-anchored: computed inner.offsetLeft = -2624 (track spans -2624..1440 at translate 0). Row1 = -2624..-592, Row2 = -592..1440. Animating to -50% (-2032px) drags both rows off to the LEFT with nothing entering from the right. Measured coverage desktop 1440: t=0 -> 1327/1440, decaying linearly to 0/1440 from t=30s to t=40s, snapping back at 42.5s. Mobile 390: 329/390 at t=0, 0/390 from t=10s to t=42.5s. 0/19 samples pass on both viewports. VERIFIED FIX: set direction:ltr on the containing block (e.g. add `.marquee-section { direction: ltr; }` in index.css, or move dir="ltr" from the inner div to the <section> in Marquee.jsx). Injecting sec.style.direction='ltr' live produced 1440/1440 coverage at ALL 19 timestamps across the full cycle (rects: row1 -87..1945, row2 1945..3977 at t=0, sliding leftwards with row2 always refilling the right side).

verified_working: @keyframes marquee-slide now ends at translate3d(-50%,0,0) (index.css line 129-132) — confirmed; max computed translate approaches -2032px on a 4064px track (desktop) and -1529px on a 3058px track (mobile), i.e. exactly one row width.
Dual-content structure intact: 1 .marquee-inner > 2 .marquee-content (2032px each desktop / 1529px each mobile), 12 .marquee-item total.
animation-name marquee-slide, duration 45s, iteration-count infinite; transform changes continuously leftwards.

No console errors on home at 1440/390 (only a pre-existing Lenis warning: 'Please ensure that the container has a non-static position...' — cosmetic, consider adding position:relative to the Lenis wrapper).
Header/hero render correctly on both viewports (screenshots); no horizontal overflow observed.
action_items: Make the marquee track LTR-anchored: add `.marquee-section { direction: ltr; }` to index.css (or set dir="ltr" on the <section> instead of the inner div in Marquee.jsx). Keep the -50% keyframe as-is. This was validated live and yields 100% coverage across the whole cycle.
Optional: add position:relative to the Lenis scroll container to clear the console warning.
critical_code_review_comments: dir="ltr" on the animated element itself does not change how the parent's RTL formatting context places an overflowing max-content block — the block's inline-start is the RIGHT edge, so overflow goes left. The direction must be set on the ancestor that establishes the containing block.

Text order inside each row is unaffected by making the section LTR because each .marquee-item's inner Arabic spans keep their own bidi resolution; visually confirmed content still rendered correctly during the live test.

Full iteration_11 regression set (fonts, cv-auto, Lenis gating, 8 blog cards, service/legal/404 routes, mobile menu, build) was already verified and was not re-run this iteration.
rca_of_the_issue: Two separate defects existed. (1) Fixed in iteration 12: keyframe end state -100% -> -50%. (2) Still open: the .marquee-inner track (width:max-content, 4064px) lives inside an RTL containing block, so it is laid out right-aligned with offsetLeft -2624; the whole track already sits to the LEFT of the viewport. A negative (leftward) translation therefore evacuates the viewport instead of cycling content in from the right, producing a 100% empty band for ~10-32s of every 45s cycle. Fix = left-anchor the track by making the containing block LTR; verified 19/19 full-coverage samples after applying direction:ltr to .marquee-section at runtime.
